script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

A quiet, spacious apartment in the heart of the city. SARAH SITTERS in a worn armchair, staring at her computer screen. Her brow furrows as she skims through job listings on the internet. She bites her lip, a frustrated sigh escaping her.

SARAH
(to herself)
Another dead end.

The door creaks open, and in walks JANE, Sarah's best friend. She carries a tray of tea and pastries.

JANE
Hey, what's got you down?

SARAH
I've been applying for jobs for months. Nothing.

JANE sets the tray on the coffee table and sits on the couch.

JANE
Have you tried networking?

SARAH
Networking? I don't know anyone in my industry.

JANE
Well, I do. I've got a friend who's a marketing manager at a tech company. She's always looking for new talent. I'll set up a meeting for you.

SARAH's face brightens.

SARAH
Really? That would be amazing!

JANE
Of course! Now, let's get you ready. We'll work on your resume, practice some interview questions, and I'll even let you borrow some professional clothes.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah and Jane sit in a corner booth, laptops open in front of them. They work quietly, Sarah typing away at her resume, Jane offering suggestions.

SARAH
(muttering to herself)
"Marketing Coordinator"... "Social Media Specialist"... "Content Strategist"...

JANE
(laughs)
You'll have a job in no time.

INT. TECH COMPANY LOBBY - DAY

Sarah, dressed in a sharp new suit, enters the lobby of the tech company. She takes a deep breath and adjusts her blazer.

SARAH
(to herself)
I can do this.

A young woman, LUCY, approaches her, a warm smile on her face.

LUCY
Hi! I'm Lucy, the marketing manager. Sarah Sitter, right? Jane gave me a heads up that you'd be coming in today.

SARAH
(nervously)
Yes, that's me. Nice to meet you.

INT. INTERVIEW ROOM - DAY

Sarah sits across from Lucy at a table, her hands folded in her lap. Lucy looks over Sarah's resume, asking questions about her experience and qualifications.

LUCY
So, Sarah, why do you want to work in marketing?

SARAH
I've always been passionate about storytelling and connecting with people. I think marketing is the perfect way to do that on a larger scale.

Lucy nods, jotting down notes on a notepad.

LUCY
Excellent answer. What skills do you have that would make you a valuable asset to our team?

SARAH thinks for a moment before answering.

SARAH
I'm a quick learner, a good communicator, and I'm very detail-oriented. I'm also very organized and can handle multiple projects at once.

Lucy looks impressed.

LUCY
I can see that. Well, Sarah, I think you'd be a great fit for our team. I'd like to offer you the job of Marketing Coordinator.

SARAH's face lights up with excitement.

SARAH
(ecstatic)
Thank you so much, Lucy! I won't let you down!

INT. TECH COMPANY LOBBY - DAY

Sarah exits the building, a spring in her step. She turns to Jane, who is waiting outside.

SARAH
(excitedly)
I got the job!

JANE hugs her friend tightly.

JANE
I knew you could do it!

INT. SARAH'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Sarah sits at her computer, typing an email to her former boss.

SARAH
(typing)
Hi [Boss],

I wanted to let you know that I have accepted a new position at XYZ Tech as a Marketing Coordinator. I will be starting on [date].

Thank you for the opportunity to work with you and the team. I have learned a great deal during my time here, and I will always be grateful for your support.

Best regards,
Sarah Sitter

She hits send, a satisfied smile spreading across her face.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
